questions.question: Which situation is best represented by the integer -8?
options: The temperature in Kelowna rose 8 °C during the afternoon.
Owen climbed 8 m up the trail at Mount Seymour.
A diver near Nanaimo is 8 m below the surface of the ocean.
Priya put $8 into her savings account.
questions.explain: A negative integer names an amount on the 'below zero' side of a starting point, so 8 m below the ocean surface is -8. The common trap is thinking any change or any loss of effort is negative — climbing 8 m up and depositing $8 are both +8.

questions.question: Order these integers from least to greatest: -7, 3, -12, 0
questions.explain: On a number line, the further left a number sits, the smaller it is, so -12 comes before -7. The most common trap is ordering negatives as if they were positive numbers (thinking -7 is less than -12 because 7 is less than 12).

questions.question: A two-colour counter model shows 9 red counters (each worth -1) and 4 yellow counters (each worth +1). What integer does the model represent?
questions.explain: Each red-yellow pair is a zero pair: 4 pairs cancel out, leaving 5 red counters, so the value is -5. The trap is adding 9 and 4 to get 13 instead of cancelling the zero pairs first.

questions.question: At 6 a.m. the temperature in Prince George was -11 °C. By noon it had climbed to 6 °C. How many degrees did the temperature rise?
questions.explain: A rise is the finish minus the start: 6 - (-11), and subtracting a negative is the same as adding, so 6 + 11 = 17 °C. The trap is dropping the negative sign and writing 6 - 11 = -5.

questions.question: Over 6 weeks, Ravi's bank balance changed by a total of -$48, and it changed by the same amount each week. What integer shows the change each week?
questions.explain: Share the total equally: -48 ÷ 6 = -8, and a negative divided by a positive is always negative, so the weekly change is -$8. The traps are dropping the sign (writing $8) or multiplying instead of dividing.

questions.question: Evaluate: -3 + 2 × (-5)
questions.explain: Multiplication comes before addition: 2 × (-5) = -10, then -3 + (-10) = -13. The classic trap is working left to right, which gives (-3 + 2) × (-5) = 5.

questions.question: Nadia's account is overdrawn, so her balance is -$18. For each of the next 3 weeks she deposits $12 from her paper route, and the bank charges her one $5 overdraft fee. What is her balance after the 3 weeks?
questions.explain: Work in order: 3 deposits give 3 × 12 = $36, so -18 + 36 = 18, then take off the one fee: 18 - 5 = $13. The traps are forgetting the fee ($18), counting only one deposit (-$11), or adding the fee instead of subtracting it ($23).

questions.question: Evaluate: (-4) × (3 - 7) - (-6) ÷ 2
questions.explain: Brackets first: 3 - 7 = -4, so (-4) × (-4) = 16 and (-6) ÷ 2 = -3, giving 16 - (-3) = 16 + 3 = 19. The biggest trap in this unit is treating - (-3) as -3 and answering 13, when subtracting a negative always means adding.
